items.reasons: At 1x this reads as a pink display shelf of polish bottles. There is no manicure table, lamp or seating, so it does not read as a nail bar. The tiny bottles in many colours (red, orange, green, purple) make a noisy confetti band across both shelves.

The ring, crossbar and base are outlined in saturated orange-gold instead of the dark navy/black outline the originals use. The navy fill inside the ring is a muddy dark blob, and the crossbar crosses over the hanging clothes with no clear depth.

The cream top plane and short front read as 3/4. The thin dark outline and muted palette match the originals. Four cubbies with clearly shaped shoes and boots read at 1x, and it sits against the wall base believably.

The wooden top is only about 1–2 rows thin, so there is no real lit top plane. The microwave fills the whole width as a flat front elevation. The red object on the lower shelf is an unreadable blob, not a recognisable appliance.

The rails and frame are drawn in straight plan (top-down) view, while the towel and shirts hang in front elevation. The mixed projection makes the rack look like a flat grate lying on the floor with clothes pasted on top.

The umbrellas are straight capsule shapes with no canopy folds or hooked handles, so they read as bottles or thermoses. The white bin has no visible open top plane, only a front box with a one-row rim.
The monitor and cart are a flat front elevation with no lit top surface. The body is full of scattered 1–2px green, black and blue specks that read as noise, not as dials and gas cylinders.

The neon emerald green with bright banded highlights is far more saturated than anything in the chipset palette. The top rail is a boxed gradient block, not a lit 3/4 plane. At one tile wide and very tall, the proportions read as a pillar, not a screen.
